anomalies.observed: The isolated CAN transceivers U15 and U43 have their logic-side ground (GND1, pin 4) and bus-side ground (GND2, pin 5) both connected to the same GND net.
anomalies.expected: For an isolated CAN bus, GND1 and GND2 must be on separate, galvanically isolated ground nets (e.g., GND and GND_ISO).

evidence.quote: two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (U8, U9) through an isolated CAN transceiver (U11/companion)

anomalies.impact: The galvanic isolation of both CAN buses is defeated. Ground loops and common-mode voltages can pass between the logic side and the CAN bus side, potentially causing communication errors or damage.

anomalies.observed: The SC16IS752 dual UARTs U33 and U48 have their I2C/~SPI mode select pin (pin 9) tied to GND, selecting I2C mode, while their SDA/VSS pin (pin 14) is also tied to GND. In I2C mode, pin 14 is the SDA data line and must not be grounded.
anomalies.expected: Either pin 9 should be tied high (VDD) to select SPI mode (in which case pin 14 is VSS and grounding is correct), or pin 14 should be connected to the I2C SDA bus if I2C mode is intended.
anomalies.impact: The UARTs are configured for I2C mode but their SDA lines are shorted to ground, preventing any I2C communication. The SPI pins (10-13) are connected to GPIOs, indicating SPI was likely intended, so the mode select pin is incorrectly tied low.

parsed.summary: The design files contain two major anomalies: the isolated CAN transceivers have their isolated and non-isolated grounds shorted together, defeating the required isolation, and the SC16IS752 UARTs are configured for I2C mode while their SDA pins are grounded, making them non-functional.

(pin (num "9") (name "I2C/~{SPI}") (type "input"))
(pin (num "14") (name "SDA/VSS") (type "bidirectional"))
In the actual SC16IS752, pin9 is I2C/~SPI. If low, I2C mode. If high, SPI mode. Pin14 is SDA in I2C mode, VSS in SPI mode. In the netlist, pin9 is on GND (low), so I2C mode.
